title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 72-74). Grothendieck gives an axiomatic characterisation of the Schwarzian derivative. Take a smooth curve X and the sheaf of local étale coordinates f, g : X -> P^1. He seeks an invariant C(f,g) with values in ω_X^{⊗2} that is:
- PGL(2)-invariant;
- a cocycle;
- given by a differential operator;
- functorial for étale maps.

In the complex case C(f,g) = -2[S(g) - S(f)] dt^2, where S is the Schwarzian. It comes with a canonical torsor T_X under ω^{⊗2} (the torsor of projective structures / projective connections) and a map c^X : P_X -> T_X. This map factors through PGL(2)\P_X and induces an isomorphism.

In (III), over arbitrary bases with divided-power derivatives D^{(n)}, the invariant is unique up to sign. The normalised form is C_0 = (1/12)C. In terms of the classical Schwarzian, C_0(g) = -D^{(3)}g/D^{(1)}g + (D^{(2)}g/D^{(1)}g)^2 = -S(g)/6, which is integral and nonzero in characteristics 2 and 3.

This page finishes Remark 1 and gives Remarks 2 and 3.

Remark 1 (end). If one allows an arbitrary coefficient sheaf F_X depending functorially on X, one is forced to have a functorial isomorphism F_X ≅ ω^{⊗2}_{X/C}, and likewise in (III). So ω^{⊗2} is the universal target.

Remark 2. The torsor T depends on the choice of C (and of F; it is a torsor under F). Different choices C and φC are canonically related: T^{φC} is the pushout ("multiple") of T^C along multiplication by φ on ω^{⊗2}. Hence the finest choice is T^{C_0}. The torsor attached to the classical C = 12 C_0 is the 12th multiple of T^{C_0}. Over Z this pushout is not invertible; in characteristics 2 and 3, 12·T^{C_0} is trivial.

Remark 3. In a fixed characteristic p > 0, conditions a), b), c) plus d') (C_0 not identically zero) characterise C_0 up to a constant in F_p^*. Over a base S the indeterminacy lies in Γ(S, O_S^*). If S is not reduced, one must impose non-triviality on each fibre k(s). The left margin note, possibly about p = 2, Witt vectors or order 3, is illegible.

The next page passes to analogous invariants for other groups, starting with translations, where A(f,g) = dg - df.
errors: "Finest" in Remark 2 must be read as: T^{C_0} determines T^{φC_0} by pushout, but not conversely when φ is not invertible (e.g. φ = 12 over Z, or in characteristics 2 and 3).
Remark 3 is cut off mid-sentence; the condition for non-reduced S is not completed on this page.

ideas.what: Universality of ω^{⊗2} as the coefficient sheaf for the Schwarzian-type invariant: any functorial F_X with such a cocycle factors uniquely through ω^{⊗2}.
ideas.modern_name: Universal property of the Schwarzian / quadratic differentials as the target of projective-structure cocycles
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Cartan, Gunning); the sheaf-theoretic universality phrasing is unclear

ideas.what: Dependence of the torsor of projective structures on the normalisation of C: T^{φC} is the pushout of T^C along φ; the integral normalisation C_0 = C/12 gives the finest torsor, and the classical one is its 12th multiple.
ideas.modern_name: Torsor of projective structures (opers for PGL2) over Z; change of structure group along multiplication by an integer
ideas.usually_credited_to: Projective connections as an ω^2-torsor: Gunning, Deligne, Beilinson-Drinfeld; integral and characteristic-p aspects: Mochizuki, Hoshi

ideas.what: Characterisation of the integral Schwarzian in characteristic p (including 2 and 3) up to F_p^*, and up to Γ(S, O_S^*) over a general base, with a fibrewise non-vanishing condition for non-reduced bases.
ideas.modern_name: Schwarzian derivative / projective structures in positive characteristic
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mochizuki (indigenous bundles, p-adic Teichmüller theory); Hoshi (projective structures in characteristic p)

missed.claim: The Schwarzian is treated over Z with divided-power derivatives. Its integral normalisation C_0 = S/6 (up to sign) is valid in characteristics 2 and 3, and the classical torsor of projective structures is 12 times the integral one. This gives a sign-unique, characteristic-free projective-structure torsor. I am not aware of this explicit axiomatic treatment being credited to Grothendieck.
missed.quote: le choix "le plus fin" de T est T^{C_0} ... le T^C correspondant de (III) est un multiple 12 ième de T^{C_0}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Projective structures and opers in characteristics 2 and 3 are delicate (Mochizuki, Hoshi, dormant opers). A canonical integral torsor whose 12th multiple is the classical one clarifies what survives at small primes.

missed.claim: The characterisation of C_0 over non-reduced bases in characteristic p is left incomplete (a fibrewise non-vanishing condition). The margin hints at an issue at p = 2, Witt vectors, or order 3.
missed.quote: Si S n'est pas réduit, il faut supposer que pour chaque k(s), l'id. ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Deformation of projective structures over Artinian or Witt bases connects to p-adic Teichmüller theory and canonical liftings.

deep.surprise_reason: These are clean, careful remarks on an integral, characteristic-free treatment of the Schwarzian and the projective-structure torsor (the factor 12 and the finest torsor). They are natural, and partly anticipated by later work on characteristic-p projective structures, but appear unpublished in this form. The main uniqueness-up-to-sign result is on the previous page.
